why: The ratchet for tools/harness/webgpuBootCheck.js. THE WEBGPU BACKEND RENDERS THE SCENE. `offscreenBytes` is how that is measured: both backends render the same scene into a private RGBA8 framebuffer and read it back, so no swap chain or compositor is involved. A flat 64x64 PNG compresses to ~200 bytes; WebGPU now gives ~5900 against WebGL2's ~6128, and the frame raises ZERO uncaptured validation errors. Raise it in the commit that earns it, never to make a red run green. It VARIES by ~100 bytes run to run (SSAO builds its kernel from Math.random at renderer construction, so no two sessions compress identically) - read it as a band, not a checksum.
blockedBy: Per-pixel accuracy, itemised per configuration in tools/harness/backendDiff.json. Twelve of twenty-five gated configurations match EXACTLY on the deferred profile and thirteen on the forward one, and nothing on either is worse than 21/128. offscreenBytes ~5910 against WebGL2's ~6010.
next: `npm run harness:backenddiff` and `:forward`, worst first. Deferred: debugCascades 17 (worst 72) is the outlier and the only one with a large delta - the cascade tint is computed inside the lighting shader rather than blitted, so it is a different code path from debugShadow, which is exact. Then a shared floor of 8-11 across base/bloom/grid/debugScene/ssao/godRays/skyFog/noShadows/halfScale/chromatic, all at worst 16-32: one cause, not ten. Forward: combined 21, then the same 8-9 floor.
history: screenQuad — new Mesh() called glDevice().createVertexArray(); the VAO is lazy now and mesh.ts went 19 glDevice() sites -> 5, all inside legacy draw paths.

preInitialize — _configureDefaultState was raw gl.clearColor/depthFunc plus a second getExtension('EXT_color_buffer_float'). The capability check goes through capabilities.floatRenderable (both backends answer it); the rest is WebGL2 standing state with no WebGPU counterpart and is guarded as such, not ported.

programs (creationSize) -> the general Texture sizing reform. `graphics/texture.ts` now syncs its dimensions into the device BEFORE every upload, and `WebGPUTexture.setSize` reallocates the GPUTexture when they change - the analogue of `reallocateBuffer`, same wrapper, new handle. The allocate-shaped calls assert the size instead of throwing.

programs (glDevice) -> Texture.bind/unbind, Mesh.initializeVAO/initializeAnimatedVAO/setupInstanceMatrixBuffer/teardownInstanceMatrixBuffer and the renderer instance buffers. All either guarded off WebGL2 (a texture unit and a VAO are concepts WebGPU does not have) or widened to the RHI Buffer interface. `_finishUpload` calling `unbind` after every upload was the sharpest of these: a legacy epilogue killing a path that had otherwise completed.

programs (gpuValidation) -> chunk 1. Texture.view returned a concrete WebGL2TextureView through an unchecked cast and WebGPU beginRenderPass reads view.handle; split into attachmentView/sampledView keyed on a new Texture.generation. _pipelineFor was building every module with source: '' and hardcoding colorTargets to rgba8unorm; both now come from the WGSL and from the target being drawn into. Plus: depth attachments honour baseArrayLayer, six epilogue unbind() calls deleted, GLState guarded and given an enum-free API (gl.DEPTH_TEST was evaluated at the CALL SITE, so guarding inside GLState could never have been enough), and the 0x0 allocation clamped so boot is not buried in ~40 async validation errors.

startup complete -> the scene now BUILDS and a frame RUNS. _setViewport and _restoreDefaultBlend were the last two raw-gl helpers on the path; guarded (a viewport is pass state on WebGPU, and a standing blend func is not a concept there). Note _setViewport still calls setViewportSize on both backends - renderStats charges fullscreen passes by area and skipping it would silently zero shadedMpx.

firstFrame (notImplemented) -> chunk 2/3. WebGPU mip generation (a blit pipeline, one pass per level per layer - 2D and CUBE together, because a cube face is an array layer and splitting the loop to defer half of it would have been more code); RenderPipeline.resources on the interface (the material bind group reached it as `(pipeline as any).module.resources`); GLState.cullFace takes a side, not an enum; Framebuffer bind/unbind guarded; TileMesh given the same lazy-VAO split as Mesh.

frame runs but submits nothing -> two instrumentation lies and two real bugs. (1) The WebGPU encoder kept NO frameStats at all, so every counter read zero and a black frame looked like "nothing drew" when it meant "nothing counted". (2) frameMs survives resetFrameStats by design, so a stale frame time sat beside zeroed counters and an empty sample looked like a finished frame. Real bugs: _checkGLErrors calls gl.getError() and the harness ENABLES debugGLErrors, so it threw every frame and the game loop (which logs and does not reschedule) died silently after the first; and index, bone and instance buffers were created without COPY_DST, which WebGL2 ignores and WebGPU rejects.

uniform bind groups bound + samplers synthesised. WebGPURenderPassEncoder.setPipeline now binds the bound program's uniform blocks (grouped BY GROUP INDEX - several blocks can share one, and WebGPU rejects a bind group whose entry count does not match its layout), and WebGPUDevice.createBindGroup synthesises the sampler entry the engine deliberately omits (it keeps filter/wrap state on the TEXTURE, which WebGL2 accepts as one combined sampler but WGSL declares as a texture+sampler pair). Both done in the backend rather than at the ~330 setUniform / _textureBindGroup call sites, which is the migration's standing constraint. Result: every bind-group validation error is gone, and the image is still blank.

blank frame narrowed by elimination, all measured on a real adapter: (1) a bare clear into an engine Framebuffer reads back 255,0,0,255, so the device pass + readback path is sound; (2) the offscreen render is 0,0,0,0 across every pixel, so it is not the transparent-background/coverage-alpha path and not the swap chain; (3) the G-buffer after a frame reads nz=1024/8192 max=60 on albedo and exactly zero on the other two attachments - and 1024/8192 is precisely what a clear to alpha=1.0 looks like in f16, i.e. the CLEAR, not geometry. Also fixed on the way: engine colour textures had no COPY_SRC, so any readback of one would have been refused (WebGL2 needs no such declaration, which is why it was invisible).

fullscreen pipelines were built with vertexLayouts: [] on the grounds that 'the shared quad still owns its own VAO' - true on WebGL2, meaningless on WebGPU, which has no VAO. The shared fullscreen vertex stage reads @location(0) position and @location(1) texCoord, so every screen-space pipeline was invalid and every draw recorded against it dropped, while the pass still performed its CLEAR. Fixed with screenQuadLayout(), which is packedModelLayout's arithmetic (the quad IS a two-attribute model vertex: stride 20, offsets 0 and 12) and returns a LIST so it can answer 'none' for a stage with no vertex attributes - a zero-stride layout is rejected. All six WebGL2 mesh baselines, both passCheck profiles and 1279 unit tests stayed green. It did NOT unblank the frame.

Blank-frame bisect, every line measured on a real adapter, not reasoned:
  PROVEN SOUND (each ruled out as the cause)
  - raw WebGPU triangle on the engine's own GPUDevice, drawn and read back: 255,0,0,255. Device,
    queue, pipeline creation, rasterisation and readback all work end to end.
  - engine Framebuffer cleared and read back: 255,0,0,255.
  - uniform writes over 3 frames: 321 calls, 321 carrying non-zero data, 165168 bytes.
  - uniform block CONTENTS: real model matrices (identity basis + translations like 1.5,0.55,1.1).
  - the GPU commands themselves: idx=3456 vbSize=35000, idx=13824 vbSize=134456, viewport default
    (full attachment). Real index counts, real vertex buffers, nothing zero-sized.
  - culling: forcing cullMode 'none' on WebGPU changed nothing, so it is not the WebGL2 bottom-left
    vs WebGPU top-left winding flip.
  - readback path: engine colour textures had no COPY_SRC. Added. Changed nothing (WebGL2 needs no
    such declaration, which is why it was invisible) - a real latent bug, not this one.
  THE SYMPTOM, stated exactly
  - G-buffer albedo after a frame: nz=1024/8192 max=60. 60 is 0x3C, and a clear to alpha=1.0 in f16
    is 0x3C00 - so that is one non-zero byte per 8, i.e. THE CLEAR AND NOTHING ELSE. The other two
    attachments are exactly zero.
  So the geometry pass runs, clears, records well-formed draws with correct data, and writes no
  fragments. What is left is between the vertex shader's inputs and its clip-space output.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND: maxBindGroups. The engine numbers bind groups by ROLE - 0 textures, 1 transform, 2 material, 3 shadows, 4 shadow uniforms, 5 lighting - so every lit program declares group 5. WebGPU's maxBindGroups DEFAULT is 4 (groups 0-3), and this adapter reports 4 as its MAXIMUM, so it cannot be raised by requesting it. Dawn rejects the pipeline: '[EntryPoint "fs_main"] infringes limits: the entry-point uses a binding with a group decoration (5) that exceeds the maximum (4)'. An invalid pipeline is not a crash - the draws recorded against it simply do nothing, while the pass still performs its clear. That is exactly and only the symptom: 101/101 draw calls counted, every bind group satisfied, correct matrices, correct vertex layouts, and not one pixel. Found by capturing the uncaptured error in JS instead of reading it in the console, which truncates it - the group numbers are in the truncated tail. The instrument that had to be fixed first: occlusion queries here return BOOLEAN any-samples-passed, not a count. A validation triangle covering 1024 samples reported 1, so an earlier reading of '1 sample per draw' as 'geometry collapsed to a point' was wrong - it meant 'samples passed'.

bind groups merged 6 -> 4, and the limit error is gone. Only the UNIFORM blocks moved: group 1 is now every uniform block, one role per binding (0 transform, 1 material, 2 shadow, 3 lighting). Every TEXTURE group stayed exactly where it was - 0 material/G-buffer maps, 2 probe cubes, 3 shadow maps - because those bind groups are built by hand in the renderer against a literal group index, while uniform blocks are bound from reflection and move for free. So the change is twelve .wgsl declarations and no renderer code. Highest group index anywhere is now 3. WebGL2 is untouched: it assigns UBO binding points from the linked program's own block index, not from the WGSL group. All six mesh baselines, both passCheck profiles, naga, uniformLayout and 1279 unit tests green.

THE GEOMETRY PASS RENDERS. G-buffer centre reads albedo nz=8192/8192 max=153 and normals nz=5067/8192 max=255 - real content, not a clear. Four fixes got there, each uncovering the next: (1) allocateDepthArray dropped its `compare` argument on WebGPU, so every shadow binding held a filtering sampler against a sampler_comparison declaration; (2) the bloom down/upsample pipelines were built ABOVE their loops, where _passTarget does not exist, so they took the rgba8unorm fallback while the mips are rgba16float - 60 of the errors; (3) ssao and deferredLighting called textureSample from non-uniform control flow (an early return, a per-pixel branch), which Dawn refuses, invalidating both modules; explicit textureSampleLevel(..., 0.0) is what the implicit form already resolved to for screen-sized un-mipped targets, LUTs and the irradiance cube. Uncaptured errors 138 -> 52. WebGL2 stayed pixel-identical throughout.

FIRST RENDERED FRAME. offscreenBytes 202 -> 3079, nonZeroPx 0/1024 -> 647/1024, scene and compose both populated (nz=7163/8192), uncaptured errors 138 -> 0. The last root cause was the depth texture: a depth-format texture cannot satisfy a `texture_2d<f32>` binding ('None of the supported sample types (UnfilterableFloat|Depth) match the expected sample types (Float)'), so the nine u_gDepth/u_coverageDepth declarations became `texture_depth_2d` and their thirteen call sites `textureSampleLevel(..., 0)` - an INTEGER level, which is what WGSL requires for a depth texture. `_samplerFor` also had to stop handing those bindings a filtering sampler, which only a comparison sampler may do. That broke WebGL2 twice over, and both are handled in tools/wgslTranslate.mjs by `fixPlainDepthSamplers`: naga renders every texture_depth_2d as `sampler2DShadow` (no textureLod overload exists for one in ES 300) and the engine knows these are non-comparison reads, so the declaration is rewritten to `sampler2D`, the level literal to a float, and `.x` appended because a GLSL sampler2D yields vec4 where WGSL yields f32. The shadow maps are texture_depth_2d_ARRAY + sampler_comparison and are deliberately untouched.

orientation fixed at its single real source: the SCREEN QUAD's V coordinates. A GL texture's v=0 is its bottom row and a WebGPU texture's v=0 is its top row, while clip space agrees in both - so a quad pairing y=-1 with v=0 puts the texture's top row at the bottom of the screen on WebGPU. Every fullscreen pass shares that quad, so one backend-conditional pair of V values fixes the whole chain rather than flipping at the end and depending on the pass count staying odd. `_encodePNG` also stopped flipping unconditionally: it exists because GL readPixels reports rows bottom-up, and WebGPU's copyTextureToBuffer already hands back the order a canvas wants. offscreenBytes 3079 -> 4935 against WebGL2's ~6100.

PER-DRAW UNIFORMS. The defect was written down in `_flushUniforms` and never acted on: `queue.writeBuffer` is ordered against the SUBMIT, not against the commands already recorded, so a pass that wrote `u_model` before each of its draws gave EVERY draw the last value written. Every check that existed passed throughout, because every one of them drew once. A `UniformSet` is an ARENA now - a buffer of slots - and a block that changed since the last draw advances to a fresh slot, so the bind group for that draw names a byte range rather than a buffer. A block that did NOT change keeps its slot, which is what stops a per-pass block (the lights, the camera, the cascade matrices) from costing one slot per draw. Bind groups are cached by the slot signature instead of by the program; the arena doubles when a pass outruns it, into a NEW buffer rather than wrapping onto a slot a recorded draw has not read yet. Cursors are released after `queue.submit` and nowhere earlier - that is the exact moment the ordering rule makes a slot free again. All ~380 setUniform call sites are untouched, which was the point. Measured: offscreenBytes 4935 -> 5175 (WebGL2 ~6135), G-buffer albedo nz 6144 -> 7090/8192. Two things had to be fixed to even RUN the gate that proves it, and both had been red on this branch for a while with nobody looking: `harness:webgpu` threw at its first `setPipeline` because `ShaderManager.bind` throws for an unregistered name and a device-tier pipeline has no engine program behind it (`bindIfRegistered` binds nothing instead, which is also the right answer - leaving the PREVIOUS pass's program bound is the failure that method's own comment describes); and the outline section still bound groups 1 and 2 long after the 6 -> 4 merge put every uniform block in group 1, so `forGroup(2)` was undefined. The new check is two draws in ONE pass with different uniforms, driven through ShaderManager + setPipeline + draw rather than by hand-built bind groups, because the aliasing lived in the encoder and a check that binds by hand cannot see it.

THE IBL BAKE WAS NEVER RUNNING. `Attachment state of [RenderPipeline "irradiance"] is not compatible with [RenderPassEncoder "iblConvolve"]` - `_convolveCubeFaces` builds ONE pipeline and then opens six passes, one per cube face, so it is the third site that has to be TOLD its target rather than leaving it to `_passTarget`; the other two (the sky-atmosphere bake, the cloud raymarch) already were, and the reason is written down at `_pipelineFor`. Without it the format came from whatever pass ran last, WebGPU refused the pipeline, and both the irradiance and prefiltered cubes held nothing but their clear - which is why the chrome sphere that samples them was the one object everybody could see was missing. WebGL2 never read the attachment formats, which is why this survived every gate on that backend. Face 0's target stands for all six: they differ only in the layer they view, and createRenderTarget dedupes. Measured: console messages 148 -> 4 with NONE of them naming a pipeline, encoder or bind group; offscreenBytes 5175 -> 5946 against WebGL2's ~6118. WebGL2 unmoved - mesh base, full and forward all green.

THE DEVICE HARNESS WAS RED AND NOBODY KNEW, because it died on its FIRST check and reported one line. Three separate faults, each hidden behind the one before it. (1) `setPipeline` calls `ShaderManager.bind(p.program)`, which THROWS for an unregistered name - and a pipeline built straight from a shader module has no engine program behind it. `bindIfRegistered` binds nothing instead, which is also the correct answer: leaving the previous pass's program bound is the exact failure `_flushUniforms` documents. (2) The outline section still bound groups 1 and 2 long after the 6 -> 4 merge put every uniform block in group 1. (3) The real one, and it reaches the RENDERER too: `createBindGroup` synthesised a sampler after EVERY textureView entry. It must do so only where the shader declares a sampler at that binding and the caller left it empty - a `textureLoad` read declares none, and a caller may pass its own. An extra entry is not a shading difference: WebGPU rejects a bind group whose entry COUNT disagrees with its layout, which invalidates the whole command buffer, so the pass does not even run its clear and the target reads back as zeros - indistinguishable from a shader that produced nothing. The declaration is read off the module's own SOURCE (`rhi/webgpu/wgslBindings.ts`), not off `descriptor.resources`, because a module can arrive without reflection. Also: the present check bound an rgba8 stand-in to `u_coverageDepth`, which has been `texture_depth_2d` since the depth-sampler commit, so it now makes a real depth texture. `harness:webgpu` went 10 FAILED -> ALL PASS, including the timestamp and compute-volume checks that had never once run.

A CROSS-BACKEND GATE, and the two bugs it found in its first run. `backendDiff.js` drives both backends through one shared configuration list (`passConfigs.js`, extracted from passCheck.js, plus the thirteen DebugView channels the baselined list never reached) and diffs the 8x8 signatures per configuration, so a difference arrives as a named channel instead of a percentage. It compares the two live runs against EACH OTHER - a recorded WebGPU baseline would freeze today's bugs as correct - and `backendDiff.json` ratchets the per-config distance downward only. `?seed=1` on the mesh page installs a deterministic Math.random BEFORE the engine is built so both renderers get the same SSAO kernel; with it the whole run is byte-reproducible across runs. Found immediately, both invisible to every existing gate: (1) `motionBlur.wgsl` called `textureSample` below an early return - non-uniform control flow - so Dawn refused the module and every motion-blur draw silently did nothing; (2) `shadowDebug.wgsl` declared the cascade array as `texture_2d_array<f32>` when it is a DEPTH format, so the bind group was invalid and the channel was blank. Fixing (2) meant generalising `fixPlainDepthSamplers` to key off the SAMPLER each depth texture is paired with rather than off the texture's own type - a `sampler_comparison` is a shadow test, a plain `sampler` is a value read - which is the rule that would have covered this case from the start. debugShadow went 72/128 -> 15/128.

PHASE C, ROUND ONE - the cross-backend gate paid for itself immediately. WebGPU was FROZEN from `debugOverdraw` onward: that pass was still on the legacy path (`gl.clear`, `gl.blendFunc`, `mesh.draw()`), `gl` is undefined on WebGPU, and the game loop logs a frame error WITHOUT rescheduling - so one visit to that channel killed the renderer for the rest of the session and every later configuration measured a stale image. The gate found it by reporting frame stats beside the signature: WebGPU submitted identical work for seventeen consecutive configurations. Moving the pass onto the RHI then uncovered the bug that had made an earlier attempt fail and be reverted, and it was NOT in `_recordDraw`: `WebGL2Device.createRenderPipeline` deduped pipelines by program, primitive, depth and colour targets - and NOT by vertexLayouts. One program legitimately draws buffers of different strides (a Basic model is 20 bytes per vertex, a PBR one 56), so the first pipeline built for a program was handed back for every later stride and `vertexArrayFor` configured every mesh at the first one. Reading a 20-byte vertex at 56 walks every third vertex, which draws it as a splayed triangle fan. It hid because the passes with that shape draw ONE object in the test scenes - the selection outline outlines a single selected node - so only one stride is ever requested; the overdraw channel draws every model in the scene, which is what finally crossed two families through one program. That fix also moved the FORWARD shading baseline by one cell, because the shadow pass draws both families through `shadowMap` and had been rasterising one of them at the wrong stride. Four more, each found by the gate and each invisible to every existing check: `outline`/`overdraw` declared three vertex attributes and use one, and WebGPU refuses a pipeline whose stage asks for an attribute the layout does not supply (WebGL2 substitutes a generic (0,0,0,1)); `debugView`'s depth channel bound a depth texture to a `texture_2d<f32>`; `volumetricGodRays` did the same and was also handed the spot-shadow array it never samples, which WebGPU's derived layout had eliminated, giving a bind group with more entries than its layout; and `findEntryPoints` scanned WGSL with comments intact, so a doc comment between `@vertex` and `fn` overran its 120-character window and dropped the stage from the translation entirely. Also: cube-face renders are vertically flipped on WebGPU - framebuffer row 0 is the bottom on WebGL2 and the top on WebGPU - which everything sampled by UV survives (the screen quad's V coordinates undo it once at present) and a CUBEMAP does not, because it is sampled by direction. Flipping `_captureProj`'s Y for the sky and IBL bakes took `base` from 67/128 to 21/128. Net: debugOverdraw, debugMetallic, debugMask, debugBloom and debugBloomMask are pixel-identical across backends; grid 117 -> 24, combined 124 -> 23, debugScene 117 -> 21, debugCascades 117 -> 17, godRays 117 -> 25.

PHASE C, ROUND TWO - five root causes, and the last of them was the forward pipeline rendering NOTHING. (1) CLEAR SCOPE: a bare `gl.clear(COLOR_BUFFER_BIT)` clears every attached draw buffer, while WebGPU clears exactly the attachments a pass names and LOADS the rest - and `_beginFullscreenPass` only ever named attachment 0, so the G-buffer's normal and emissive targets kept the previous frame on one backend and were wiped on the other (debugRoughness 65 -> 0, debugAO 67 -> 0). (2) CLIP DEPTH: WebGL2's clip volume is -w..w and it stores (z/w+1)/2; WebGPU's is 0..w and it stores z/w. Every projection here is the GL-convention form, so WebGPU stored a different number for the same geometry. Depth TESTING never noticed - it is a comparison - but SSAO, god rays, fog, motion blur, cloud occlusion and the depth channel all READ that buffer. `_clipProjection` multiplies by z'=(z+w)/2 on WebGPU, whose NDC z EQUALS what WebGL2 stores, so the buffers now hold identical values and no shader changed (debugDepth 62 -> 0, debugShadow 15 -> 0). (3) SCREEN-SPACE Y: the shared quad pairs clip y=-1 with v=0 on WebGL2 and v=1 on WebGPU, so the relationship between `in.uv` and clip space is MIRRORED - and every reconstruction spells it out as `uv*2-1`. Folded into the matrices instead of into a dozen shaders: matrices that CONSUME a uv-built clip vector are post-multiplied by diag(1,-1,1,1), matrices that PRODUCE one to be read back as a uv are pre-multiplied (debugSSAO 78 -> 0, ssao 61 -> 10, combined 17 -> 4). (4) STANDING CLEAR COLOUR: 'no clearValue' meant 'whatever gl.clearColor was last set to', which WebGPU has no equivalent for, so those passes cleared to transparent black there (debugEmissive 55 -> 0, debugNormal 49 -> 0, debugAlbedo 54 -> 4). (5) THE FORWARD PIPELINE WAS BLANK: `_renderScene` opened with a raw `gl.clear`, which threw on WebGPU, and the game loop logs a frame error without rescheduling - one clear-coloured image and then nothing, for the rest of the session. The diff named it without ambiguity: all 29 configurations reporting the same 69 draws and ZERO fullscreen passes is a renderer that stopped, not 29 shading differences. Forward went from 0 of 25 matching, every one at 116/128, to 13 of 25 exact. Also fixed on the way: `WebGPUTexture.uploadBytes` took three parameters where the interface declares four, silently dropping the address mode - TypeScript permits it - so the SSAO rotation noise was clamped instead of repeating.
